([[Mishawaka, Indiana]]) * [[La Lumiere School]]
([[La Porte, Indiana]]) | college = [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] (2020–2022) | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2022]]) * First-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] (2022) * [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] All-Freshman Team (2021) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 Latvia]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Jaden Edward Dhananjay Ivey''' (born February 13, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue Boilermakers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Ivey grew up playing [[American football|football]], [[basketball]] and [[association football|soccer]] and practicing [[karate]]. He started focusing on basketball as a freshman in high school.{{cite web |last1=Hunsinger Benbow |first1=Dana |title=The remarkable story of Purdue's Jaden Ivey and his mom, Notre Dame coach Niele Ivey |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/purdue/2021/02/25/purdue-basketball-freshman-jaden-ivey-and-mom-notre-dame-niele-ivey/4510097001/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=May 21, 2021 |date=February 25, 2021}} Ivey played for [[Marian High School (Mishawaka, Indiana)|Marian High School]] in [[Mishawaka, Indiana]] in his first three years.{{cite web |last1=Noie |first1=Tom |title=Former Marian standout Jaden Ivey is a new player, and new person, at LaLumiere |url=https://www.southbendtribune.com/sports/high_school/basketball/former-marian-standout-jaden-ivey-is-a-new-player-and/article_539735d2-37da-11ea-ab6a-ffc2e4a512e5.html |website=[[South Bend Tribune]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=January 16, 2020}} For his senior season, he transferred to [[La Lumiere School]] in [[La Porte, Indiana]], joining one of the top programs in the country.{{cite web |last1=Skol Jr. |first1=Mark |title=Jaden Ivey 'became a man' in senior season at La Lumiere |url=https://www.wndu.com/content/sports/Jaden-Ivey-became-a-man-in-senior-season-at-La-Lumiere-570049351.html |website=[[WNDU-TV]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=April 29, 2020}} A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] over offers from [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]].{{cite web |last1=Baird |first1=Nathan |title=Purdue basketball receives first 2020 commitment from Mishawaka Marian's Jaden Ivey |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2019/04/24/mishawaka-marians-jaden-ivey-commits-purdue/3566430002/ |website=[[Journal & Courier]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=April 24, 2019}} ==College career== [[File:Jaden Ivey.jpg|thumb|left|Ivey in January 2021]] Early in his freshman season, Ivey missed five games with a foot injury.{{cite web |last1=Carmin |first1=Mike |title=Energetic Jaden Ivey returns to Purdue basketball after dealing with foot injury |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/2020/12/18/energetic-jaden-ivey-returns-purdue-basketball-after-dealing-foot-injury/6543793002/ |website=[[Journal & Courier]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=December 19, 2020}} On January 19, 2021, he made a game-winning three-pointer with five seconds left as part of a 15-point performance in a 67–65 win over [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].{{cite web |last1=Brew |first1=Tom |title=Jaden Ivey Gets Emotional After Hitting Game-Winning 3-Pointer for Purdue |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/jaden-ivey-hits-game-winning-three-pointer-purdue-beats-ohio-state |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=January 20, 2021}} On March 19, Ivey scored a season-high 26 points in a 78–69 overtime loss to [[North Texas Mean Green men's basketball|North Texas]] at the first round of the [[2021 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]].{{cite web |last1=Pells |first1=Eddie |title=North Texas comes up big with 78-69 upset over Purdue |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-thomas-bell-javion-hamlet-mens-college-basketball-purdue-boilermakers-mens-basketball-147dc487afc23aadfcfe3c6181f36243 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=March 19, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 11.1 points and 3.3 rebounds per game, earning [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |last1=Skol Jr. |first1=Mark |title=Former local high school basketball star Jaden Ivey named to Big Ten All-Freshman team |url=https://www.wndu.com/2021/03/09/former-local-high-school-basketball-star-jaden-ivey-named-to-big-ten-all-freshman-team/ |website=[[WNDU-TV]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=March 9, 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Schutte |first1=Dustin |title='We've got unfinished business': Jaden Ivey explains decision to return to Purdue |url=https://saturdaytradition.com/purdue-football/weve-got-unfinished-business-jaden-ivey-explains-decision-to-return-to-purdue/ |website=Saturday Tradition |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=April 27, 2021}} On November 12, 2021, Ivey scored 27 points in a 92–67 win over [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]].{{cite news |title=Ivey, Edey help No. 7 Purdue steamroll Indiana State 92–67 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401372164 |access-date=January 28, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 12, 2021}} On January 30, 2022, he scored 21 points and hit the game-winning three-pointer with 0.6 seconds remaining in an 81–78 win over [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].{{cite news |title=Ivey 3 in last second, No. 6 Purdue fends off No. 16 Ohio St |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364412 |access-date=January 30, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 30, 2022}} As a sophomore, he averaged 17.3 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game. Ivey was named to the First Team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] as well as the All-American Second Team.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|title=2021-22 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} On March 31, 2022, Ivey declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Carmin |first=Mike |title='This has been a lifelong dream of mine' Purdue's Jaden Ivey declares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2022/03/31/purdue-sbasketball-ophomore-jaden-ivey-nba-draft-nba-lottery-pick/7235032001/ |access-date=2022-03-31 |website=Journal and Courier |language=en-US}} He is a projected top five pick in the draft.{{Cite web |title=Jaden Ivey |url=https://nbadraftroom.com/jaden-ivey/ |access-date=2022-03-31 |website=NBA Draft Room |language=en-US}} ==National team career== Ivey played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Latvia.{{cite web |last=Fezler |first=D. J. |title=Purdue Basketball's Jaden Ivey to Wear No. 9 for the USA U-19 Team |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/purdue-basketballs-jaden-ivey-to-wear-no-9-for-the-usa-u-19-team |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=June 28, 2021}} On July 3, 2021, he scored a team-high 21 points, shooting 7-of-11 from the field, in a 83–54 group stage win over [[Turkey men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Turkey]].{{cite web |last=Fezler |first=D. J. |title=Jaden Ivey Leads USA U19 FIBA World Cup Team to Victory, Caleb Furst Logs Seven Points |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/jaden-ivey-leads-usa-u19-fiba-world-cup-team-to-victory-caleb-furst-logs-seven-points |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=July 3, 2021}} Ivey averaged 12.3 points per game, helping his team win the gold medal, and was named to the all-tournament team.{{cite web |last1=Fezler |first1=D. J. |title=Purdue's Jaden Ivey, Zach Edey Named to FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup All-Star Team |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/purdue-jaden-ivey-zach-edey-named-to-fiba-u19-basketball-world-cup-all-star-team |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 11, 2021 |date=July 11, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] | 23 || 12 || 24.2 || .399 || .258 || .726 || 3.3 || 1.9 || .7 || '''.7''' || 11.1 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] | '''36''' || '''34''' || '''31.4''' || '''.460''' || '''.358''' || '''.744''' || '''4.9''' || '''3.1''' || '''.9''' || .6 || '''17.3''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 59 || 46 || 28.6 || .440 || .322 || .739 || 4.3 || 2.6 || .8 || .6 || 14.9 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Ivey's mother, [[Niele Ivey]], serves as head women's basketball coach at [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish women's basketball|Notre Dame]].{{cite web |last1=Fortuna |first1=Matt |title=For Niele and Jaden Ivey, this basketball season strengthens a mother-son bond |url=https://theathletic.com/2401563/2021/02/22/niele-jaden-ivey-notre-dame-purdue-college-basketball/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=May 21, 2021 |date=February 22, 2021}} She played in the [[Women's National Basketball Association|WNBA]] for five seasons and was an [[NCAA Women's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] player at Notre Dame. Jaden’s father, [[Javin Hunter]], played for the [[Baltimore Ravens]] and [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the [[National Football League|NFL]]. His grandfather, [[James Hunter (American football)|James Hunter]], also played in the NFL for the [[Detroit Lions]].{{cite web |last1=Berardino |first1=Mike |title=Jaden Ivey's Notre Dame roots help vault him up the 2020 basketball recruiting lists |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/notre-dame/notre-dame-insider/2019/02/18/notre-dame-roots-help-jaden-ivey-vault-him-onto-2020-basketball-recruiting-radar/2907455002/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=May 21, 2021 |date=February 18, 2019}} Ivey has one brother, Jordan Hunter. Ivey is a [[Christian]].{{cite web |last1=Mercer |first1=Kevin |title=Purdue star Jaden Ivey, mother Niele bonded by faith as both experience NCAA Tournament success |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/basketball/2022/03/21/purdue-jaden-ivey-mother-niele-faith/ |website=Sports Spectrum |access-date=March 23, 2022 | date=March 21, 2022}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://purduesports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jaden-ivey/10676 Purdue Boilermakers bio] *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/i/ivey-jaden.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{2022 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Ivey, Jaden}} [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from South Bend, Indiana]] [[Category:La Lumiere School alumni]] [[Category:Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]]
